predictions_reviewed.reason: I agree with the label, but the answer gives the weaker reason. It relies on selection: the register records decisions. There are two stronger reasons. (a) Every observed change starts from no authorization and ends in an authorization, and creating an authorization needs an authorizing act on either hypothesis (SQ6). (b) Under R-A3 the act and the after-state are the same record (AC1). There is also the hypothesis reading. If H-B's 'in response to work' can mean acts that work triggers, H-B predicts exactly what H-D predicts, and P1 cannot discriminate even in principle. The only place in the corpus where a change without an act could appear is the contingent authorization in R-72 becoming operative. That transition is not observed (SQ4).

predictions_reviewed.status: CONFOUNDED (a candidate anomaly against H-B, n=1)
predictions_reviewed.favours: neither; weakly against H-B if the confound resolves toward non-conformance
predictions_reviewed.reason: This is a one-sided test. H-D makes no prediction, so only H-B is at risk. The answer overstates the timing confound (SQ5): R-77 ('REMAINS BLOCKED', after 'R-73–R-76 stand') and R-79 (RED only after the two Board acts, which were still OPEN on 08-04) make it likely that the norm in force at R11 was 'blocked'. What remains confounded is (i) whether RED tests that leave producers 'deliberately unnamed' fall under what is blocked, and (ii) the unobserved acts R-76, R-78 and R-80. The answer also leaves out execution-side observations from the source text: R-94 'Executed at IMPLEMENTATION_PROGRESS.md:58' (a Chief disposition carried out with no adoption by the Decision Authority), R-86 'engineering waiting solely on a constitutional act' (which reads as conformance), and S0804 'Nothing implemented this turn by the review's own instruction' (also conformance). None of these is coded as an execution record.

The answer itself says the observed feedback 'does not discriminate, because H-D accommodates acts that cite evidence'. A prediction on which the two hypotheses are observationally equivalent is NON-IDENTIFIABLE. Calling it PARTIALLY IDENTIFIED is a labelling error. The answer also misses more act-mediated feedback cases: R-41, where the WP-1 closure inconsistency leads to ES-004.3 and 'first checklist execution ... caught a second instance ... annotated', and S0815, where O-CLOSURE-VOCAB leads to the 'BINDING VOCABULARY RULING' and then 'Applied immediately'. These add to the count but do not change the verdict.

predictions_reviewed.status: NON-IDENTIFIABLE (as a discriminator); H-D's clause is corroborated, n=2, by self-report
predictions_reviewed.reason: H-B does not deny status mediation, so observing it cannot tell the hypotheses apart. The answer admits this and still gives the label PARTIALLY IDENTIFIED. The count is 2 (E1 and E3), not 1. In both, force is 'observed' only through declarations inside the norm-making acts ('These become governing rulings effective immediately'). That is the same kind of evidence the answer rejects for P1, where it says R-77's clause 'shows the actors endorse H-D's rule. It does not show that the rule holds' (CI2). R-89 remains an unresolved possible falsifier of H-D.

H-B is silent, so P5 cannot discriminate. The same labelling error applies as for P4. R-94 remains open as a candidate falsifier of H-D. But the domain itself offers a reading under which R-94 is no exception: the Decision Authority held that operational acceptance is not a constitutional decision (R-90). That points to a scope question, not a capability breach.

The answer says the result depends on where the record's boundary is drawn. It does not. H-B predicts that the record carries OR references work, and even the narrowest boundary (register rows only) references and reports work: 'Executed at IMPLEMENTATION_PROGRESS.md:58', 'Container resolution executed and reproduced', the grep in R-83, 'first checklist execution the same day caught a second instance'. So H-B's prediction is met at every boundary. H-D says work 'need not' be in the record, which permits its presence. The two are observationally equivalent on what is present. The answer's line 'draw the boundary at the register and it matches H-D's self-description' is wrong (LP1).

predictions_reviewed.status: CONFOUNDED (with the R-89 status question); on act versus no act it reduces to P1
predictions_reviewed.reason: The answer says 'nothing is observed about whether WP-4B was accepted' by R-89. That is too strong. There is positive indirect evidence, not merely an absence. The same day, R-86 authorizes batch-7 execution, and acceptance comes after RED → GREEN → VERIFY (R-72, R-79). R-89 itself says '§WP-4 remains OPEN'. So R-89 very probably authorized WP-4C-1 before WP-4B was accepted, against R-72's gate (INFERENCE, strongly supported). Whether that counts against H-B depends on whether R-89 ever took force. It is PREPARED, yet the Decision Authority says 'R-89 already governs authorization'. That is the confound.

I agree with the label. But the answer says 'the corpus ends on 2026-08-04', which is false: S0815 is a session log dated 2026-08-15. The absence of any later R-91 remediation is still a limitation of the corpus, but the window is misstated. S0815 contains further failure-and-remediation pairs that the answer does not use: O-CLOSURE-VOCAB is found and 'Recommended as its own work item', 'E-2 is CORRECTED (seq 18)', and a forbidden headline is 'corrected, not defended'. All of these go through an act, so they fit both hypotheses.

discriminating_observation_types.overall: No prediction is IDENTIFIED on this corpus, and neither hypothesis is favoured. The reason is structural. H-D makes no prediction about work (P2, P3, P6), and H-B, read as allowing acts triggered by work, is compatible with every act-based claim of H-D (P1, P4, P5, P8). So the hypotheses come close to being nested, and only two kinds of observation could separate them: (i) a verified norm change with no act, which would falsify H-D's 'only'; or (ii) verified non-conformance, or verified absence of feedback, which would count against H-B. The corpus has no case of (i). It has candidates for (ii): R11 against R-72, R-77 and R-79, and R-89 against R-72's acceptance gate. Both are confounded, the first by what the block covers and by unobserved acts, the second by R-89's PREPARED status. Neither is resolved. The answer reaches the same bottom line, but it rates P3, P4 and P5 too high and P2 and P7 too low.

critique_of_draft.overall: The specifications are useful, and they name the right missing records (R-73..R-80 text, R-87/R-88, R-89's adoption status). Four of them fail the test of sufficient and minimal. (1) The P4 and P5 specifications cannot discriminate, because H-B has no falsifier; asking for 3 episodes only corroborates H-D. (2) The H-D falsifier for P1 requires a 'complete act log ... including unregistered ones', and absence of an unregistered act can never be shown. (3) Several H-B falsifiers have no time window ('no later sanction') or rely on attitudes ('actors must treat these as normal'). (4) Episode minimums of 3 are set without a stated reason.
